title: Kth Largest
description: Easy: sort descending and index k-1. Optimal interview answer: size-K min-heap → O(n log k). See the Implement Min-Heap lesson for the heap primitive.

notes: Default .sort() is lexicographic — ALWAYS pass a comparator for numbers.
`(a, b) => b - a` sorts DESCENDING; `a - b` ascends.
For the optimal interview answer, drill the MinHeap lesson — then this becomes a 4-line streaming solution.
Quickselect averages O(n) and is what staff-level interviewers expect; min-heap is the safe middle ground.

questions.q: After `nums.sort((a, b) => b - a)`, where is the kth largest?
Why pass a comparator instead of bare `.sort()`?
options: Default sort coerces to strings — [10, 2].sort() gives [10, 2] not [2, 10]

questions.q: Time complexity of the sort-based solution?
For very large n where k is small, the best asymptotic approach is:
options: Sort the whole array — O(n log n)

exercises.prompt: Sort descending and return the kth-largest by index.

blanks.hint: kth largest sits at index k - ?

L3.prompt: Write `findKthLargest(nums, k)` using the sort approach. Log `findKthLargest([3,2,3,1,2,4,5,5,6], 4)`.
hints: Sort DESCENDING with `(a, b) => b - a`.
Return the element at index k - 1.
